long_biography.plain_text:
Crimestoppers is the clearest institutional expression of Lord Michael Ashcroft's philanthropy. He founded the charity in 1988 after the murder of PC Keith Blakelock revealed how fear could stop witnesses approaching police. Its anonymous reporting model has since become a permanent channel for people unable or unwilling to identify themselves to law enforcement.

Ashcroft also founded the school that became Ashcroft Technology Academy and supported business education at Anglia Ruskin University. His lifelong interest in gallantry produced the world's largest collection of Victoria Crosses, displayed publicly for fifteen years at Imperial War Museums. Together, these projects place education, crime prevention and the preservation of individual courage at the centre of his public legacy.
